text:
Tyson Foerster played only 29 games last season, and the Flyers have spent the first month of this one waiting for the shooter they remember. Seven points in 21 games, four goals on 5.1 expected, shooting about 9%: The Philadelphia Inquirer argued this week that the slow start is par for the course for him, and the numbers lean that way.

His shot is still elite (NHL Edge has his hardest in the 96th percentile), and the goals tend to catch up with the chances. Three goals and three assists in his last ten, including a power-play goal against Edmonton, suggest it's starting. On Saturday in Columbus, Charlie O'Connor of PHLY Sports singled out his work off the wall setting up Trevor Zegras and wrote that Foerster "needs to get that back in his game."

The bigger worry is the five-on-five play. Philadelphia takes only 42% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) with him on the ice, close to the team's poor overall level. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking shows he dumps the puck in on most entries, so his line lives on the forecheck. When that works, the shot does the rest.
